identity.title: LER 2023-001-01 for Prairie Island Nuclear Generating Plant, Units 1 and 2, Reactor Trip, Auxiliary Feedwater and Emergency Service Water System Actuation due to Electrical Transient in DC Control Power Cables

cause.proximate_text: the directional drilling equipment traveled through a DC cable bundle containing control cables, causing damage which resulted in the opening of multiple substation breakers in the switchyard leading to a Unit 1 Turbine Trip and subsequent Reactor Trip. The root cause of this human performance issue was weakness in the Excavation Permit approval process as well as the inadequate oversight of the non-nuclear supplemental workers performing HDD work.
cause.theme: Inadequate excavation permit review and contractor oversight leading to underground cable strike

nodes.display_name: Substation breakers (including Unit 1 generator output breaker)
Directional drilling equipment struck DC control cable bundle
nodes.description: HDD boring equipment traveled through a DC cable bundle containing control cables, causing physical damage.

nodes.display_name: Multiple grounds detected on DC control cabling for both Units
nodes.description: Damage to DC control cable bundle resulted in multiple grounds on control cabling from plant to substation control house.
Electrical transient from damaged DC control cables caused multiple substation breakers, including the Unit 1 generator output breaker, to open.
Loss of generator output breaker led to turbine trip.
Turbine trip resulted in subsequent reactor trip.
Turbine trip caused 1M Main Transformer, normal power supply to NSR busses on Unit 1, to become deenergized.

nodes.display_name: 1R Auxiliary Transformer deenergized, unavailable for Fast Bus Transfer
nodes.description: 1R Auxiliary Transformer was also deenergized as a result of the event and therefore was not available for a Fast Bus Transfer.

nodes.display_name: Loss of all NSR busses on both Units
nodes.description: Loss of 1M and unavailability of 1R for Fast Bus Transfer resulted in loss of all non-safety-related busses on both Units.

nodes.display_name: Steam Generator Water Level rapidly shrank below AFW auto-start setpoint
nodes.description: Reactor trip resulted in SGWL in both Steam Generators rapidly shrinking to below the setpoint for automatic AFW pump start.

nodes.display_name: Automatic actuation of both AFW pumps (11 Turbine Driven, 12 Motor Driven)
Loss of NSR 11 Cooling Water Pump
nodes.description: Loss of all NSR busses on Unit 1 resulted in loss of the 11 Cooling Water Pump, dropping CL header pressure.

nodes.display_name: Automatic start of 121 MDCLP on low CL header pressure (ESW actuation)
Replace damaged DC control cables; abandon existing cables in place; install equivalent conduits/cables
Initiate procedure changes to address gaps in non-nuclear supplemental worker oversight and Excavation Permit approval process

nodes.title: De-energization of 2RY Transformer due to opening of wrong Reserve Auxiliary Transformer disconnect switch, causing auto-start of 121 Motor Driven Cooling Water Pump
nodes.plant: Prairie Island Nuclear Generating Plant, Unit 2

chain: excavation permit review/oversight weakness [cause TBD] -> HDD equipment strikes DC control cable bundle -> multiple grounds on DC control cabling & substation breakers open -> Unit 1 turbine trip -> reactor trip -> SGWL shrinks below setpoint -> AFW pumps auto-start; parallel: 1M/1R transformers deenergized -> loss of all NSR busses -> loss of 11 CL pump -> 121 MDCLP auto-starts (ESW actuation)
notes: Cause code is TBD/provisional per FORM-366 fields despite a detailed root-cause narrative (Excavation Permit approval weakness and inadequate HDD contractor oversight); category kept as 'provisional' per rule 4. Two previous similar events described in narrative: the Oct 17, 2021 event has a citable LER number (50-282/2021-002-00, recorded as key '1-2021-002-00' per unit-digit convention) and is modeled as a stub LER with SIMILAR_TO edge; the Oct 17, 2023 event (two days prior) is not assigned an LER number in the narrative and is not modeled as a stub node to avoid fabricating a key. Fast Bus Transfer and safety system responses (AFW, ESW) performed as designed per Assessment of Safety Consequences -- no BACKED_UP_BY edges asserted since AFW/MDCLP are actuated consequences, not backups. SFP cooling (121/122 SFP pumps) mentioned only in safety-consequence assessment with no impact and is treated as design/consequence context, not modeled as a System/Component node.
